div.head: Attachment B
div.p: SOME LONG-TERM SECURITY OBJECTIVES IN JAPAN

list.item: A militarily strong Japan able to defend its own territory and willing and able to use its forces abroad for the defense of free world nations.

Japanese membership in an over-all regional security pact, or in related bilateral or limited security pacts, capable of providing collective security for the entire free world position in the Far East.

Continued United States military presence in Japan to the extent required by the existing situation, with the right to utilize military bases in Japan in order to fulfill our commitments for the defense of the free world.
Japanese agreement to the introduction of nuclear weapons into Japan.
A Japan with a strong economy capable of maintaining a high level of employment with a rising living standard, and good morale, and providing the substructure for necessary armament.

A Japan where economy is geared to the maximum beneficial extent with the economies of the free Asian and other free world countries,
including a Japanese contribution of skills, technology, capital and capital goods to the economic growth and development of the underdeveloped countries.

note.p: Dulles commented on these objectives in a March 23 memorandum to Robertson concluding that “The essential, it seems to me, is that the Japanese should accept the basic premise that their future lies in close cooperation with the United States to create a balance of power as against the Soviet Union and Communist China.” (Department of State, PPS Files: Lot 67 D 548, Japan)
